title: Create final lifecycle growth sprint readout + present to GTM/Product
creator: Henry Cho
description:
Goal
Produce the final sprint readout for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (emails + console nudges + retargeting), align stakeholders on decisions (ship/iterate/rollback), and present in the cross-functional readout.

Primary audience
GTM + Product + Eng/Design stakeholders who need a single source of truth for: (1) what we launched, (2) results vs baseline, (3) guardrails, (4) decisions and next actions.

Scope
1) Build readout doc (using the sprint readout template).
2) Pull final metric tables + screenshots (dashboards and console states).
3) Summarize learnings + decision recommendations.
4) Run stakeholder review and incorporate edits.
5) Present 25-min readout + 15-min Q&A; circulate recording + final doc.

Activation definition (for this sprint)
Primary: first_request_success (first 2xx completion) within 72h of signup.
Secondary (high-intent): first_streaming_success; dashboard_viewed (latency/cost); billing_added; create_route/deployment; invite_teammate.
Notes: PM-412 decision was to use first 2xx completion for primary activation to avoid biasing toward streaming-only users; streaming remains a key diagnostic/high-intent step.

Data sources
- Experiment tracker (variant IDs, targeting rules, start/stop dates)
- Activation funnel dashboards (by segment, region, SDK)
- Email platform reports (deliverability, open/click/unsub)
- Support/Jira volume + top categories
- Console performance/SLO dashboard

Readout content outline (final)
1) Executive summary (1 slide equivalent)
- What we changed (3 levers)
- Net impact on activation + early retention
- Decisions (ship/iterate/pause)
- Key caveats + next sprint bets

2) Baseline + taxonomy sanity
- Baseline funnel (signup -> api_key_created -> first_request_success -> D7)
- Event coverage + known instrumentation issues and fixes

3) Experiment results (by lever)
A) Onboarding email sequence (self-serve new signups)
- Variant: Email v1 (5-email series) vs control
- Primary metric: activation within 72h
- Secondary: time-to-first-success, api_key_created rate, support link clicks
- Deliverability/unsub guardrails

B) Console onboarding nudges (checklist + 2 banners)
- Variant: nudge v1 vs holdout
- Primary metric: activation within 72h
- Secondary: dashboard_viewed, first_streaming_success, error->success conversion
- Product guardrails: console perf (p95), error rate

C) Retargeting (non-activated + lapsed)
- Primary: activated within 7d of click (or first_request_success)
- Secondary: CTR/CVR, cost per activated user, assisted conversions
- Guardrails: claims substantiation links, landing page bounce

4) Guardrails and incidents
- Any unsub spikes, suppression issues, support ticket deltas, SLO regressions
- What we did to mitigate (rollbacks/hotfixes)

5) Decisions + rollout plan
- What stays on by default
- What remains behind flag / continues to iterate
- What is paused

6) Learnings + next sprint backlog
- Top blockers remaining (by qualitative + data)
- 3–5 prioritized follow-ups with owners and dependencies

Final results summary (included in readout)
- Emails: +5.8pp activation within 72h (directionally consistent across US/EU; strongest for TypeScript SDK users). Time-to-first-success improved by ~14% median. Unsub remained within guardrail (0.18% vs 0.20% threshold). Decision: ship Email v1 as new default for self-serve new signups; continue A/B subject lines only.
- Console nudges: +3.1pp activation within 72h (largest lift in users who created a key but stalled before first request). Banner focused on “copy-paste curl” had highest downstream success; checklist step completion correlated with D7. No measurable SLO impact on console p95. Decision: roll forward checklist + 1 banner; iterate/retire the “enable streaming” banner copy (high impressions, low completion).
- Retargeting: CTR acceptable but CVR-to-activation below target; high variance by audience. Decision: pause lapsed-user spend; keep non-activated signup audience with refreshed creative that points to troubleshooting + minimal ‘hello inference’ snippet; revisit with improved landing page variant.

Caveats (called out explicitly)
- One instrumentation hotfix mid-sprint (missing sdk_language property on first_request_success events) affected early slices; final analysis excludes impacted window for SDK breakdown and uses corrected data post-fix.
- Attribution: retargeting assisted conversions likely undercounted for users who later activated directly in console (cookie loss). Use product-event-based activation as primary; treat ad platform conversions as directional.

Deliverables
- Final readout doc link (with screenshots and tables)
- 1-page exec summary (pasteable into email/Slack)
- Recording link + Q&A notes
- Follow-up backlog list (Linear links)

Meeting
- Title: Lifecycle Growth Sprint Readout (Week 3)
- Duration: 40 minutes (25 + 15)
- Presenters: Ben Carter (results + GTM actions), Henry Cho (metric definitions + decisions), Marissa Cole (console changes + rollout plan)
- Attendees: Growth, MOPs, Product, Eng, Design, CS/Sales, Exec sponsor
acceptance_criteria:
1) Readout doc completed with: hypothesis, experiment setup, results tables, guardrails, interpretation, decisions, and next steps.
2) All primary metrics tie back to canonical events (event-taxonomy doc) and the analysis plan (PM-415).
3) Stakeholders have reviewed and signed off (see checklist) before the presentation.
4) Presentation completed; recording and final links posted in #general and relevant functional channels.
5) Next-sprint backlog items created/updated in Linear with clear owners.
stakeholder_review_checklist:
- Growth (Ben Carter): results narrative + GTM actions reflected accurately; confirm what ships vs iterates
- Marketing Ops (Tyler Benson): attribution notes, UTMs, suppression/deliverability summary, compliance notes
- Product Console (Marissa Cole): console nudge decisions + rollout/rollback plan behind flags are correct
- Telemetry/Experiment requirements (Paula Mendes): metric definitions, randomization units, and exclusions match PM-415
- Design (Tessa Morgan): screenshots/copy shown in readout match what shipped; accessibility concerns called out if any
- Engineering (Jada Williams / Jin Woo Park): experiment assignment/holdout interpretation is correct; known instrumentation issues documented
- SLO/Guardrails (Sean Gallagher): console performance/SLO chart included; confirm ‘no regression’ call
- Support/CS (Dev Patel / Aparna Reddy): support ticket deltas are correctly summarized; top blockers list matches reality
- Sales feedback loop (Avery Johnson): approved language for inbound questions included in appendix/FAQ
- PMM (Soojin Lee): claims/benchmarks are substantiated with links; no over-promising
- Exec sponsor (Camila Reyes): executive summary reflects final decisions and asks
presentation_plan:
Pre-reads (send 24h prior): readout doc + 1-page exec summary.

Agenda (40m):
1) Exec summary (5m)
2) What launched + exposure (5m)
3) Results by lever (15m)
4) Guardrails + incidents (5m)
5) Decisions + next steps (5m)
6) Q&A (5m)

Post-meeting: publish final doc + recording; open thread for follow-ups; ensure owners assigned for next-sprint items.
comments: 2025-01-22 (Ben Carter): Please make sure the exec summary has a crisp ‘ship/iterate/pause’ table. We need clarity for next sprint planning + comms to Sales/CS.

2025-01-28 (Tyler Benson): Attribution caveat: ad platform conversions won’t match product activations; please anchor on product events and include UTM coverage notes. Also include suppression incident (SUP-2849) and final fix status.

2025-02-03 (Marissa Cole): For console nudges, call out that rollout stayed behind feature flag (onboarding_nudges_v1) and we kept a 10% holdout for measurement. Include rollback steps and current exposure %.
2025-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): Need one slide/table on console perf guardrails (p95 TTI + error rate). We had no regression but want it explicit. Also include any support-link click spikes as a signal.
2025-02-10 (Soojin Lee): Please remove any absolute latency claims from the retargeting section unless we link to the benchmark page. OK to say ‘Redwood-verified performance profiles’ + link.

2025-02-12 (Aparna Reddy): Top remaining blockers to highlight: API key permissions confusion, model selection confusion (‘which model should I pick’), and streaming disconnect errors. Recommend next sprint includes a troubleshooting-first flow and better error copy.
